justification: A production DB write that changes what the capacity engine serves per zone, plus a CI wiring change. Directionality (calibration rule 2026-08-12): the write REMOVES a control from zones it does not apply to, so the failure mode is a missing control, not an invented number - but the filter is skip-only, so a wrong tag deletes a correct control, which is why all 76 candidates were read individually rather than batched by regex.

break_it.scenario: A row reads 'within 800m station or 400m B3/B4' and is tagged zone_specific because a regex saw a zone code.
break_it.what_happens: The control is PROXIMITY-based. Tagging makes the skip-filter drop it for every property not zoned B3/B4 - deleting a correct parking rate from the zones that actually use it. Silent: the report renders with one fewer control, no error.
break_it.how: All 8 canada_bay rows excluded by id. Tagging is driven by an explicit adjudicated id list, never by the regex.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-32b  # 0; the 17 excluded ids are listed in the probe comment

break_it.scenario: A clause reference like '(C1.1.9(e))' or 'Table C2.2' is read as zone C1 / C2.
break_it.what_happens: Same deletion, on Waverley and Wingecarribee POS and site-coverage controls.
break_it.how: 7 such rows excluded by id with the matched text recorded in the probe comment.

break_it.scenario: Row 52 is secondary_dwelling_specific; overwriting applicability could drop it from the granny-flat product.
break_it.what_happens: applicability is single-valued, so zone_specific destroys the secondary-dwelling meaning.
break_it.how: Both consumers fall back to dev_type: conveyancing_db.py:461 (is_sd) and granny_flat.py:211 (OR dev_type='secondary_dwelling'). Asserted pre-commit that row 52 still has dev_type='secondary_dwelling'.

break_it.scenario: The UPDATE touches rows outside the adjudicated list.
break_it.what_happens: Unreviewed controls silently vanish from zones.
break_it.how: Single transaction; asserted rowcount == 59, zone_specific 24 -> 83 exactly, DQ-32b 76 -> 17 exactly, and all 17 excluded ids still untagged - all BEFORE commit. Backup dcp_setback_controls_dq32b_backup_20260812.

break_it.scenario: Widening the probe regex instead of excluding by id.
break_it.what_happens: A NEW row naming a zone without the tag would stop being reported - the check would go quiet exactly when drift appears.
break_it.how: Exclusions are an id allowlist. The pattern is unchanged, so new rows still fail.

break_it.scenario: The four grounding checks are wired in and one of them fails the build.
break_it.what_happens: gates goes red on an observation-mode check that has not earned blocking status.
break_it.how: continue-on-error: true, and each invocation is `|| echo ::warning::`. All four exit 0 today regardless of findings.

verified: Served output re-derived through the real filter: penrith/dwelling_house/landscaping_min returned [35,40,40,50] in EVERY zone; now R2 -> [50], R4 -> [35].
canada_bay RFB car_parking unchanged in both zones, confirming the 8 proximity exclusions took effect.
sutherland_shire RFB car_parking now returns nothing in R2 - correct, those 4 rows are R3/R4 only and RFBs are not permitted in R2. Empty is a supported state in this path.
python scripts/dq_check.py: PASSED, 0 red, 13 checks across 56 rows.
DQ-57 probe added and returns 346 of 668 (exit 1, declared open - the ratchet agrees).
gaps: 44 of 56 ledger rows still have no check. Recorded in dq_checks.json why_no_check, not claimed as coverage.
DQ-32 (562) is untouched and its probe ignores applicability entirely, so it cannot see that 40 of the tagged rows are now zone-resolvable. The count will not move.
The zone filter's hardcoded list still omits R6/E2-E4/RU*/IN*/SP*/W*/B3-B8 and cannot parse negation. Both affect 0 rows today; measured, not assumed.
The four grounding checks now RUN but nothing reads their output on a schedule. Promotion to blocking still requires someone to look.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Exits 1 whenever ANY current, non-review row names a zone code in its condition text while carrying an applicability other than zone_specific, excluding the 17 adjudicated ids. Falsifiable in both directions and both were exercised: it returned 76 before the write and 0 after, and dq_check.py's bidirectional ratchet ALSO fails if the row is declared fixed while the probe is non-zero, which is exactly what caught the tracker row still reading OPEN during this change. It cannot be satisfied by loosening the pattern, because the exclusions are an id allowlist - a new zone-naming row still fails.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The count comes from the live database, not from anything this change asserts. The served-output verification re-derives values through the real filter body at scripts/conveyancing_db.py:412-418 rather than trusting that tagging had the intended effect.

pre_impl.existing_data: 76 candidate rows in dcp_setback_controls, read individually rather than counted. applicability held universal_residential x69, development_specific x5, sepp_cdc_only x1, secondary_dwelling_specific x1. Existing zone_specific rows: 24. ses_study_lga, needed for DQ-57, is NOT a column in any table - it is nested inside property_reports.outputs, found via information_schema after a guessed flood_assessments table did not exist.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The headline '76 rows to tag' was wrong and tagging all 76 would have caused a silent regression. The filter is SKIP-ONLY, so a wrong tag deletes a correct control rather than adding a wrong one. 17 rows are not zone-specific at all: 8 encode PROXIMITY ('within 800m station or 400m B3/B4'), 7 matched clause or table references, 1 a road classification, 1 has a fallback clause, 1 uses the zone for a sub-case. A second assumption also failed: 'DQ-32b overlaps DQ-32 so the 562 will drop' - it will not, because the DQ-32 probe ignores applicability entirely.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new surface. The zone filter, the probe registry and the ledger all already existed; this adds an id allowlist to one probe, one probe entry for DQ-57, and one CI step invoking four scripts that were already written and merged in #874/#876. The four were found by sweeping scripts/ against gates.yml and .githooks/pre-push, not assumed absent.
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the live DB were unreachable the probe exits 2, which dq_check.py reports as UNKNOWN rather than clean - the distinction that turned main red on 2026-08-12 and was fixed in #939.

functions.name: dq_probe_live.PROBES['DQ-32b']
functions.what: Counts current, non-review setback controls whose condition names an NSW zone code while applicability is not zone_specific, minus 17 adjudicated ids.
functions.edge_cases: Clause references (C1.1.9), table references (Table C2.2) and proximity phrasing all match the zone pattern but are not zone membership; each is excluded by id with its reason recorded on the line above it.
functions.failure_mode: Returns 0 while a genuinely untagged row exists only if that row's id were added to the allowlist, which is a visible diff.
functions.output: int count of untagged zone-naming rows, plus the SQL that produced it
functions.if_none: Exit 2 (UNKNOWN), never 0. A probe that cannot reach its source is not a clean probe.

functions.name: dq_probe_live.PROBES['DQ-57']
functions.what: Counts flood property_reports whose nested ses_study_lga came back JSON null.
functions.edge_cases: Uses jsonb_path_exists/jsonb_path_query_first rather than a LIKE, so there is no '%' for psycopg2 to mis-escape and the nested key is read directly rather than by string match.
functions.failure_mode: Reports 0 if the key is renamed upstream; the paired jsonb_path_exists guard makes that visible as a drop in the denominator (668).
functions.output: int count of flood reports whose ses_study_lga came back null, out of 668 carrying the lookup
functions.if_none: Exit 2 (UNKNOWN). If the nested key is absent everywhere the denominator drops to 0, which is visible rather than silent.

functions.name: fetch_dcp_setbacks
functions.what: Returns the DCP setback/landscaping/parking controls for one council, dev type and zone. Its zone filter (lines 412-418) skips a zone_specific control when the condition names zones and the property's zone is not among them - the consumer of the tag this PR sets.
functions.edge_cases: Substring match on a hardcoded 10-code list; cannot parse negation. Both measured as affecting 0 rows today, so neither was changed in this PR.
functions.failure_mode: Skip-only, so its failure mode is a MISSING control, never an invented one. This is why a wrong tag is the dangerous direction.
functions.input: lga_slug, zone_code (e.g. 'R2 Low Density Residential'), dev_type
functions.output: list of setback/landscaping/parking control dicts for that zone only
functions.if_none: Returns an empty list, which is a supported state this path already renders as 'not available'. Verified: sutherland_shire RFB car parking in R2 now returns nothing, correct because those rows are R3/R4 only.

post_merge.db_reset: No migration and no schema change. The write is an UPDATE of applicability on 59 rows, reversible from dcp_setback_controls_dq32b_backup_20260812 with UPDATE dcp_setback_controls c SET applicability = b.applicability FROM dcp_setback_controls_dq32b_backup_20260812 b WHERE c.id = b.id.
post_merge.secrets: None added or read. The probes reach the DB through scripts/dq_db.py, which resolves DATABASE_URL from the main checkout's .env and opens the session read-only with a 30s statement timeout.
post_merge.other_repo: None. All four newly wired scripts already live in this repo; no submodule, no external service, no companion repo is touched.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open a Penrith dwelling-house capacity result on an R2 property and confirm landscaping shows 50% alone rather than four competing values, then an R4 property showing 35%. Then confirm a Canada Bay RFB still shows its parking rates, which proves the 8 proximity rows were NOT tagged. After the next few gates runs on main, read the 'Output grounding (OBSERVATION ONLY)' step's log to start accumulating the false-positive record that blocking status depends on.
